prompt: Loading a user's orders takes 3 seconds. The query plan shows a full table scan for WHERE user_id = ?.
trap: One slow query, not many queries.

prompt: A query filters by status and sorts by created_at. An index on status alone still sorts millions of rows.
tells: filters by status and sorts by created_at
why: Use a composite index (status, created_at) that serves both filter and sort.
trap: Column order in the index matters.

prompt: Lookups by LOWER(email) are slow even though email has an index.
why: Wrapping the column in a function skips the index; add an expression index on LOWER(email).
trap: The index exists but doesn't match the query.

prompt: A table with 14 indexes has fast reads but inserts have become slow.
why: Every index costs on writes; drop unused ones.
trap: Indexes are a trade-off, not free speed.
